entries.what: Shows which files you have changed, which are ready to be saved (staged), and which files git is not tracking yet.
entries.when: Before you add or commit, and any time you want to check where you are.

entries.what: Creates a new branch called my-change and moves you onto it, so your work stays separate from the main version.
entries.when: At the start of any new piece of work, before you edit files. Pick a short name that says what the change is.

entries.what: Marks every changed file to be included in your next commit. The dot means "everything in this folder".
entries.when: After git status shows only the changes you expect. To pick one file instead, use git add followed by the file name.

entries.what: Saves the staged changes as one snapshot in your local history, with a short message saying what and why.
entries.when: When a small, working piece is done. Several small commits are easier to review than one huge one.

entries.what: Sends your branch to GitHub. The -u part remembers the link, so next time plain git push is enough.
entries.when: The first time you push a new branch, so it shows up on GitHub and can become a pull request.

entries.what: Downloads new commits from GitHub and merges them into the branch you are on.
entries.when: Before you start work for the day, and whenever someone says they pushed something you need.

entries.what: Lists the last five commits, one line each, newest first.
entries.when: To remember what you did last, or to find the commit someone is asking about.

entries.what: Creates a folder called .venv holding its own copy of Python and its own packages, so this project’s installs cannot break other projects.
entries.when: Once per project, the first time you set it up.

entries.what: Makes your terminal use the Python and packages inside .venv. Your prompt shows (.venv) while it is on. Type deactivate to switch it off.
entries.when: Every time you open a new terminal to work on the project, before running its code or tests.

entries.what: Reads the project’s list of required packages and installs them into the active toolbox.
entries.when: Right after activating a fresh .venv, and again whenever requirements.txt changes.

entries.what: Runs every automated test in the project and prints a short summary. -q means quiet: fewer lines, same result.
entries.when: Before you commit and before you open a pull request, to prove you did not break anything.

entries.gloss: run some tests, stop at the first failure
entries.what: -k picks only tests whose name contains the word you give (here "lookback"). -x stops at the first failing test so you can fix it before going on.
entries.when: When one thing is failing and you want a fast loop on just that test.

entries.command: Open a pull request on GitHub (Compare & pull request)
entries.gloss: ask for your branch to be reviewed
entries.what: A pull request asks the team to look at your branch and, once approved, merge it into main. GitHub shows the changes, the checks and the conversation in one place.
entries.when: After you have pushed your branch and the tests pass. Never merge your own work without the owner’s say-so.

entries.what: Lists the files your branch changed compared with main, with a count of added and removed lines.
entries.when: Just before opening a pull request, to check you are not sending anything you did not mean to.

entries.gloss: who is on the private network
entries.what: Lists the devices on our private network (the tailnet) and whether each is online.
entries.when: Before opening the Kibana or Shuffle links. If you are not connected, those pages will not load.

entries.what: Prints this device’s private tailnet address.
entries.when: When someone needs to reach your machine over the tailnet. Keep the address out of chat and public repos.

entries.what: Shows the lines you added and removed in files that are not staged yet. Plus means added, minus means removed.
entries.when: After editing and before git add, to review your own work. Use git diff --staged to review what is about to be committed.
entries.goal: Learning how to check my edits before committing
